warnings: First, verify the liquid surface is actually being rendered: ensure the baked liquid mesh object exists and is visible in render (not hidden), and that the domain cage isn’t the only thing assigned the water material.
Make the leak readable: increase secondary spray/whitewater (spray droplets) and ensure they are visible at frame 40; add motion blur if needed so the jet reads as continuous.

Improve puddle readability: ensure a thin puddle covers the cabinet floor with strong grazing-angle specular; add a visible meniscus at the front lip and 1–2 hanging droplets to sell the start of dripping.
Fix lighting/exposure: reduce blown highlights and strengthen the warm-vs-cool lighting separation so wet reflections clearly show warm pendant highlights plus cool LED accents.
Tighten water material: clear transmission with correct IOR behavior and very low roughness for sharp highlights; avoid milky/diffuse look unless simulating dirty water.
Add wall wetness/rivulets: use wet maps or shading variation to create darker wood streaks and glossier runoff paths where the jet hits and flows downward.
